exceptions.rationale: The lock boundary must cover the entire effective viewport before the ordinary application shell is available; this is a viewport relationship, not reusable control or card spacing.
The recovery surface needs a wider readable measure for provider diagnostics and protection-boundary copy while remaining constrained by the viewport.
The protection warning uses a bounded reading measure for consequential confirmation copy; its width is page composition and does not define reusable dialog padding or control geometry.
The keyboard shortcut list has a compact content-specific reading measure while the shared dialog surface continues to own its padding, border, radius, and scrolling behavior.
The durable-task confirmation needs a bounded desktop measure plus an explicit small-viewport gutter; the shared dialog primitive owns all generic surface geometry.
One physical pixel is part of the established visually-hidden accessibility clipping recipe and must not be replaced by a spacing token that could expose hidden text.
The negative one-pixel margin is inseparable from the visually-hidden accessibility clipping recipe and is not application spacing or visual composition.
One physical pixel is part of the established visually-hidden accessibility clipping recipe and must not be replaced by a spacing token that could expose hidden text.
Dialog height is intentionally related to the effective viewport so the shared surface owns contained scrolling and preserves a canonical tokenized outer gutter.
Application data tables preserve a minimum readable cell measure and contain excess width in the focusable table region; spacing, borders, and row geometry remain tokenized.
